verdict.reasoning: Patient reports itchy, dry, widespread rash: 'I've noticed my skin is sore and red... It's all over my chest, my hands and arms... It's very itchy and dry.' Duration 'over the past few days.'

Eczema is extensive and involves chest, hands, inner elbows and is itchy/dry: 'It's all over my chest, my hands and arms, especially inside of the elbows... It's very itchy and dry.' Doctor later says 'it looks like... quite widespread, your eczema.'
Transcript states no weeping but presence of cracks: Patient: 'Is it weeping?' Doctor: 'No.' Patient later: 'Okay. Right. Yeah. So you have cracks over there.' Fact incorrectly states no cracking.
No thickened skin: Patient asks, 'Is there any thickened skin...?' Doctor: 'No. No, I don't think. I don't think so.'
History of eczema and current episode worse: Doctor: 'Yes, I have Eczema in the past.' and 'I think it's gotten worse. Like this past few years. Days.' which indicates worsening compared to prior.
Limited effect of cetirizine: Doctor: 'I realized I've tried also antihistamines and didn't work.' Patient clarifies 'like cetrazene? Yeah, yeah, yeah.'

No fever implied in 'feeling well' and no temperature: Patient: 'Otherwise, other than those rash, you're feeling well in yourself, there's no temperature...?' and there is no disagreement by the doctor, implying no fever.
No joint pains: same sentence, 'there's no temperature, no joint pains?' followed by 'Yeah, no joint pain.'
History of asthma: Doctor: 'I have asthma.'
History of eczema: Doctor: 'Yes. Yes, I have Eczema in the past.'
Emollients used: 'Usually I use a cream called Dipro Base. In the shower. I use something called Dermal.'
Over-the-counter hydrocortisone: Patient asks if hydrocortisone rings a bell, 'Yeah. So you're using the hydrocortisone? Yeah.'
Over-the-counter cetirizine: Doctor: 'I realized I've tried also antihistamines and didn't work.' Patient: 'Okay, so like cetrazene? Yeah, yeah, yeah.' and 'The one over the counter.'
Blue inhaler as needed: Patient: 'what medications are you using for asthma?' Doctor: '...the blue inhaler.' Patient: 'you just use it on and off?'; Doctor: 'Yeah, yeah, yeah.'
No known allergies: 'Do you have any allergies to any medication at all?' Doctor: 'No, no allergies.'
Same as drug allergies: 'Do you have any allergies to any medication at all?' Doctor: 'No, no allergies.' so no drug allergies are documented.
Mother with hypothyroidism: 'Who has hypothyroidism?' Doctor: 'My mother.'
Mother has migraine: 'in my family there is hypothyroidism and migraine. My mother has migraine.'
'No fever or joint pains' matches: 'you're feeling well in yourself, there's no temperature, no joint pains? ... Yeah, no joint pain.'
Distribution and description: 'It's all over my chest, my hands and arms, especially inside of the elbows... It's very itchy and dry.' and to weeping: 'Is it weeping?... Doctor: 'No.''
No thickened skin: 'Is there any thickened skin...?' Doctor: 'No. No, I don't think. I don't think so.'
Breathing stable: Patient: 'But your breathing's all okay? Yeah.' Doctor: 'Okay. Yeah, yeah. It's only when I have a flare.'
'Uses a blue inhaler as needed' restates asthma medication usage: 'the blue inhaler' and 'you just use it on and off? ... Yeah, yeah, yeah.'

Atopic dermatitis/eczema flare with extensive involvement and pruritus: clinician: 'it looks like... quite widespread, your eczema' and patient describes 'very itchy and dry' rash over chest, hands, arms, inner elbows.

Asthma on as-needed SABA: 'what medications are you using for asthma?... the blue inhaler.' and 'you just use it on and off? ... Yeah, yeah, yeah.' and 'But your breathing's all okay? Yeah.' This supports well-controlled asthma on as-needed blue inhaler (short-acting beta agonist).
No drug allergies documented: 'Do you have any allergies to any medication at all? ... No, no allergies.'

Start fexofenadine: 'you would probably need some antihistamines which I'm going to prescribe... It's called the antihistamine it's called fexofenadine.' Dose frequency 'one dose daily' is not explicitly stated but daily use is implied; still acceptable as direct clinical inference.

Betamethasone topical (Betnovate) twice daily for 2 weeks: 'You might probably need a bit more stronger one like betno weight or something like that... we will try with some Bettner weight first... You have to use it twice a day for the next couple of weeks.' Betnovate is a betamethasone-containing steroid; 'couple of weeks' ≈ two weeks.

Continue emollients: 'You still need to continue on your emollients like the dermal soap and as well as the depravate. Yeah. So you still need to use those in the interim.' Dipro Base and Dermal were earlier named; 'Depravate' appears as another product. Instruction to continue them is explicit.
Contact clinic if no improvement or adverse reaction: 'If there's no improvement, you need to get back to us. Or if you have any kind of adverse reaction... you need to get in touch with us.'

Prescription to Boots: 'we are going to send off the prescription to your pharmacy. It looks like Boots on the systems, is that correct? ... So I'll send it across to Boots and it will be there for collecting.'

Return if worse or not improved in two weeks: 'If things are getting worse in the next two weeks, call us beforehand. Otherwise, wait for two weeks, take the medication and the cream.' This covers worsening and lack of improvement timeframe.

Transcript advises to call if worse or no improvement but does not explicitly schedule or state a planned reassessment visit in two weeks; 'wait for two weeks' does not guarantee a booked reassessment.
